directions: Plant divisions in moist, humus-rich, well-drained soil in partial to full shade, where the deeply and sharply lobed foliage will slowly knit together into a dense groundcover mat. Cutting Edge is named for its distinctively jagged, almost fern-like leaf margins, marked with a bold dark maroon central zone that intensifies in cooler weather, and is topped by fluffy white to pale pink bottlebrush flower spikes in mid-spring. Like other modern tiarella introductions it spreads gently by stolons rather than aggressively, making it well suited to woodland edges and shaded rock gardens. Keep soil consistently moist, since foliage can scorch during dry spells in too much sun.

planting.note: Divide established crowns or plant nursery divisions in spring in humus-rich, moisture-retentive but well-drained soil in partial to full shade; a named clonal fern selection, propagated by division rather than spores to remain true to type.

directions: Divide established crowns or plant nursery divisions in spring in humus-rich, moisture-retentive but well-drained soil in partial to full shade. Widely regarded as one of the finest hardy fern cultivars in cultivation, this selection forms a majestic, upright shuttlecock of fronds clothed in golden-brown scales, with each frond tip and pinna elegantly crested, giving the whole plant a formal, architectural presence. It holds a Royal Horticultural Society Award of Garden Merit and remains substantially evergreen to semi-evergreen through mild winters. Site it as a specimen or anchor plant in a shaded border where its bold texture and crested form can be appreciated up close.

planting.note: Plant divisions in spring in cool, moist, well-drained, humus-rich soil in partial to full shade, ideally sheltered from drying winds; a named clonal fern selection, propagated by division rather than spores to remain true to type.

directions: Plant divisions in spring in cool, moist, well-drained, humus-rich soil in partial to full shade, ideally sheltered from drying winds. This is among the most finely dissected soft shield fern cultivars available, with fronds so densely and repeatedly divided that they take on a soft, feathery, almost moss-like texture unlike any other hardy fern. Evergreen in all but the harshest winters, it holds a Royal Horticultural Society Award of Garden Merit and is prized by fern collectors for its exceptionally refined texture in a shaded rockery or woodland setting. Remove tattered old fronds in late winter just before the new crosiers unfurl.
